item.description:

The stories in this piece are related by fictional characters in historical situations, through spoken word and dance, with an original score. Cast of 11. Oct 16 at 7pm, Oct 17 at 5pm, Oct 18 at 3pm. CONTENT WARNING This production shows graphic images of violence, including warfare, bombings, and their victims, with intense, jarring audio of gunfire and explosions. item.title: Montclair Film Festival - Kill. Bury. Print. — Sat Oct 17, 8:00 PM — The Wellmont Theater
item.description:
KILL. BURY. PRINT. tackles brazen corruption and press intimidation in remote southeast Oklahoma. When a small family-run newspaper begins reporting on allegations of sex, drugs, and violence within the county sheriff’s office, they find themselves the target of the sheriff’s retaliation. As tensions escalate, the paper secretly records the sheriff and local officials musing about killing and burying them, turning a local story into national news. Ben Klein’s film is a timely and powerful story of the relationship between journalists and those in power, a look at how corruption threatens our access to the truth. Q&A with Director Ben Klein and Producer Rachel Maddow follows the screening. Share this: Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook

item.title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes) — Wed Oct 28, 11:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.
There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.
Source: Meetup: The Mindful Stream

item.title: Mapping the Election: The Impact of Historic and Modern Maps on the Midterms NEW — Wed Oct 28, 6:15 PM — Montclair Bellevue Ave Branch - Kids Place
item.description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.
All eyes are on the midterm elections, and maps--both old and new--not only show how people vote but often help set and reinforce the patterns of how citizens are divided. First we'll take a look at maps of gerrymandering, which started in Massachusetts in 1811 and have taken very specific forms in the United States because of the rules of the American political system. We'll move onto the familiar red and blue election maps and examine how they privilege big, sparsely populated states like Wyoming over dense locations like New Jersey. We'll also take quick looks at great historical images, like Civil War-era election maps whose sectional splits look shockingly modern.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306
